docs.description: Chief Executives and Managing Directors are senior organisational leaders responsible for determining and directing the overall strategy, policy, and operational objectives of an enterprise or organisation. They provide high-level leadership across all business functions, ensuring alignment between corporate goals and day-to-day operations. This role typically sits at the apex of an organisation's management structure and may involve accountability to a board of directors, shareholders, or other governing bodies.

ai_draft.description: Chief Executives and Managing Directors are senior organisational leaders responsible for determining and directing the overall strategy, policy, and operational objectives of an enterprise or organisation. They provide high-level leadership across all business functions, ensuring alignment between corporate goals and day-to-day operations. This role typically sits at the apex of an organisation's management structure and may involve accountability to a board of directors, shareholders, or other governing bodies.
typical_tasks: Determine and communicate the organisation's strategic direction and long-term objectives.
Oversee the development and implementation of organisational policies and procedures.
Direct and coordinate the activities of senior management and departmental heads.
Monitor financial performance, budgets, and resource allocation across the organisation.
Represent the organisation in negotiations, partnerships, and public engagements.
Report to and liaise with boards of directors, shareholders, or governing bodies.
Ensure regulatory compliance and risk management frameworks are maintained.
Lead organisational change initiatives and drive continuous improvement programs.
Evaluate and approve major capital expenditure and investment decisions.
Foster organisational culture, stakeholder relationships, and corporate governance standards.
ai_draft.qualification_rules:
Candidates assessed under ANZSCO 111111 are typically expected to hold a relevant bachelor's degree or higher qualification in business, management, commerce, or a related field. Extensive senior management experience, often spanning multiple years in progressively responsible leadership roles, is generally considered integral to satisfying assessment requirements. In many cases, substantial practical experience at an executive level may be considered alongside or in lieu of formal qualifications, subject to the assessing body's discretion.

The Institute of Managers and Leaders National (IML National) is the nominated skills assessing body for this occupation in Australia. Applicants should consult IML National's current assessment criteria directly, as requirements regarding documentation, referee reports, employment evidence, and recognition of prior learning may vary. No specific fees or processing timeframes are stated here, as these are subject to change and must be confirmed with IML National and the relevant visa authority.
ai_draft.ai_confidence_note: Admin must verify: the current ANZSCO occupation group classification, confirmation of IML National as the active assessing body, and whether 111111 appears on the MLTSSL and/or CSOL in the current official instrument.

snapshot.title: Chief Executive or Managing Director
snapshot.description: Chief Executives and Managing Directors are senior organisational leaders responsible for setting strategic direction, overseeing operational performance, and ensuring an enterprise meets its financial, regulatory, and stakeholder objectives. Working within frameworks established by a board of directors or ownership group, they translate high-level policy into executable business plans and drive organisational culture. This occupation encompasses leadership roles across private, public, and not-for-profit sectors and is classified under ANZSCO code 111111.
typical_tasks: Determine and articulate the organisation's strategic vision, goals, and long-term plans.
Oversee day-to-day operations and ensure alignment with board-approved objectives.
Report to and liaise with the board of directors on organisational performance.
Manage senior leadership teams and delegate responsibilities across business units.
Monitor financial performance, budgets, and risk management frameworks.
Represent the organisation in negotiations with major clients, partners, and government bodies.
Ensure compliance with relevant legislation, regulations, and corporate governance standards.
Lead organisational change initiatives and drive continuous improvement programs.
Approve major capital expenditure, contracts, and policy decisions.
Build and maintain relationships with key external stakeholders and industry bodies.
snapshot.qualification_rules:
Candidates are typically expected to hold a bachelor's degree or higher qualification in business administration, commerce, management, or a closely related discipline. Postgraduate qualifications such as an MBA or equivalent are common and may strengthen an application; however, extensive senior management experience at an executive or equivalent level is generally weighted heavily alongside formal education.

The assessing body for this occupation is the Institute of Managers and Leaders National (IML National). Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate a sustained history of executive-level leadership, accountability for organisation-wide outcomes, and evidence that their role involved genuine strategic authority rather than operational management alone. Skills assessment requirements, including documentation standards and experience thresholds, should be confirmed directly with IML National and against current Department of Home Affairs guidelines prior to lodgement.

ai_draft.description: A Fruit or Nut Grower plans, establishes, and manages the cultivation of fruit and nut crops for commercial production. This occupation involves overseeing all stages of the growing cycle, from soil preparation and planting through to harvesting, pest and disease management, and post-harvest handling. Fruit or Nut Growers may operate independently on their own land or manage production operations on behalf of a farming enterprise, applying both practical agricultural knowledge and sound business management skills to maximise yield and product quality.
typical_tasks: Plan and prepare land for fruit or nut crop planting, including soil testing and amendment
Select and source appropriate cultivars suited to local climate and market requirements
Establish and maintain irrigation systems to manage crop water requirements
Monitor crops for pest, disease, and weed activity and implement control strategies
Apply fertilisers and soil conditioners in accordance with crop nutrition programs
Prune, train, and thin fruit trees or nut plants to optimise yield and quality
Organise and supervise harvest operations, including labour and equipment scheduling
Oversee post-harvest handling, grading, storage, and dispatch of produce
Maintain farm records including production data, chemical use, and financial accounts
Ensure compliance with relevant food safety, environmental, and workplace health and safety standards
ai_draft.qualification_rules:
Australian skills assessments for this occupation are conducted by Vocational Education and Training Assessment Services (VETASSESS). Applicants are typically assessed against a combination of formal qualifications and relevant work experience. Relevant qualifications may include Certificate III or IV level programs in horticulture, agriculture, or a closely related field from the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) or an assessed overseas equivalent. Applicants without formal qualifications may still be considered if they can demonstrate substantial, verified work experience in a closely related role, though the specific requirements are subject to VETASSESS guidelines.

Work experience should be directly relevant to the management and operation of fruit or nut growing enterprises. Both pre and post-qualification experience requirements may apply depending on the level and field of the qualification held. Applicants are strongly advised to consult the current VETASSESS assessment criteria and obtain a professional skills assessment prior to lodging any visa application.
ai_draft.ai_confidence_note: Admin must verify the current ANZSCO classification details for code 121213, confirm VETASSESS as the assessing body, confirm inclusion on the Regional Occupation List (ROL), and check that no MLTSSL or STSOL listing applies, against official DIBP/Home Affairs and VETASSESS sources.

ai_draft.description: Software Engineers design, develop, test, and maintain software systems and applications to meet user and organisational requirements. Working across various domains including enterprise systems, embedded software, web platforms, and mobile environments, they apply engineering principles to produce reliable, scalable, and maintainable code. Software Engineers typically collaborate with cross-functional teams including analysts, architects, and project managers to deliver technology solutions aligned with business objectives.
typical_tasks: Analyse user and system requirements to define software specifications and architecture.
Design, code, and implement software applications using appropriate programming languages.
Conduct unit, integration, and system testing to identify and resolve defects.
Review and debug existing codebases to improve performance and reliability.
Prepare and maintain technical documentation including design specs and API references.
Collaborate with stakeholders to refine requirements and communicate technical constraints.
Apply software engineering methodologies such as Agile, Scrum, or DevOps practices.
Manage version control and participate in code review processes.
Contribute to the deployment, monitoring, and maintenance of software in production environments.
Research emerging technologies and recommend improvements to existing systems and processes.
ai_draft.qualification_rules:
The Australian Computer Society (ACS) is the nominated assessing body for this occupation. Applicants are generally expected to hold a bachelor's degree or higher in a closely related ICT field, or a non-ICT degree accompanied by a graduate-level ICT qualification or substantial relevant work experience. ACS assesses qualifications against its defined skill categories and may consider Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) pathways for applicants whose formal qualifications do not closely align with the nominated occupation.

Work experience is an important component of the skills assessment. Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate a history of employment tasks that align directly with the ANZSCO definition of Software Engineer (261313). ACS applies its own assessment criteria, which may include consideration of the relevance of the field of study, the level of qualification, and the recency and duration of employment. Applicants should consult the ACS website for current assessment requirements, as policies and documentation standards are subject to change.
